newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pakhoed buys 51 pct of U.S. Wilmington.
newsitem.headline: Pakhoed buys 51 pct of U.S. Wilmington.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping group Pakhoed NV said on Monday it had bought a 51 percent stake in Wilmington Liquid Bulk Terminals Inc in the U.S.
Wilmington Liquid Bulk Terminals is based near Los Angeles at the port of Long Beach. It has two terminals with capacity of 2.4 million barrels to store chemical and petroleum products.
This acquisition complements Pakhoed's ability to serve an expanded customer base in North America, the Dutch group said adding the takeover would immediately contribute to its results.
"Opportunities for further growth are available with the expansion potential on both terminals," Pakhoed said in a statement.
The current deal, of which no financial details were given, raises Pakhoed's U.S. operations to a total of 18 facilities, 13 of which handle liquid bulk storage and distribution.
Two Pakhoed units in the U.S. handle dry bulk storage and distribution and the remaining three are active in environmental services.

Up to now, Wilmington Liquid Bulk Terminals was a part of the Keystone/Kurz Group. This Pennsylvania-based group of companies is active in deep sea domestic and intercoastal transport including storage of bulk liquids.
